1	package store
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"sort"
6		"strings"
7		"sync"
8	)
9	
10	type Kind int
11	
12	const (
13		KindUnknown Kind = iota
14		KindRecord
15		KindBlob
16		KindLink
17	)
18	
19	// Item is one entry the loader tracks.
20	type Item struct {
21		ID    string
22		Kind  Kind
23		Owner string
24	}
25	
26	// Metadata is what the loader knows about an item beyond its ID.
27	type Metadata struct {
28		record Record
29		labels map[string]string
30		blobID string
31	}
32	
33	type Loader struct {
34		mu    sync.Mutex
35		items map[string]*Item
36		meta  map[string]*Metadata
37	}
38	
39	func NewLoader() *Loader {
40		return &Loader{items: map[string]*Item{}, meta: map[string]*Metadata{}}
41	}
42	
43	var errNoBlob = errors.New("item has no blob id")
44	
45	func (l *Loader) Track(it *Item) error {
46		md, err := loadMetadata(it)
47		if err != nil {
48			return err
49		}
50		l.mu.Lock()
51		defer l.mu.Unlock()
52		l.items[it.ID] = it
53		l.meta[it.ID] = md
54		if md.record.Owner != "" {
55			it.Owner = md.record.Owner
56		}
57		return nil
58	}
59	
60	func (l *Loader) Forget(id string) {
61		l.mu.Lock()
62		defer l.mu.Unlock()
63		delete(l.items, id)
64		delete(l.meta, id)
65	}
66	
67	func (l *Loader) IDs() []string {
68		l.mu.Lock()
69		defer l.mu.Unlock()
70		ids := make([]string, 0, len(l.items))
71		for id := range l.items {
72			ids = append(ids, id)
73		}
74		sort.Strings(ids)
75		return ids
76	}

units.headline: Adds 5-minute TTL for remembering failed inventory lookups
units.summary: Adds errorCacheTTL = 5m, which sets how long any failed GetRecord stays cached. The comment says it is for permanently forbidden records, but the TTL applies to every kind of error.
focus: Whether 5 minutes is acceptable for transient errors, which this TTL also covers, not only FORBIDDEN
units.reason: New TTL constant controls how long lookup failures suppress server calls.

units.headline: New unexported cachedError type stores error and expiry
units.summary: Plain unexported struct holding an error and its expiry time. GetRecord is where it is used and where the logic lives.
units.reason: Plain unexported data holder; the behavior lives in GetRecord.

units.headline: Client gains error cache map and injectable get/now funcs
units.summary: Adds an errors map plus get and now function fields so tests can swap them. The errors map is never swept, and like the existing cache it has no locking.
focus: The errors map grows with every distinct failing key and is never swept
No mutex on the maps while Track/loadMetadata run outside the Loader lock

issues.title: Unsynchronized error map adds to existing data race
issues.failure_scenario: Two goroutines call Loader.Track at the same time; loadMetadata runs before l.mu.Lock, so both write c.errors/c.cache at once and Go throws a fatal concurrent map write.

units.reason: Struct gains new state that changes lookup behavior.

units.headline: NewClient initializes error map and wires default get/now
units.summary: Initializes the new errors map and sets get to fetchFromServer and now to time.Now. This simply wires up the new fields.
units.reason: Straightforward initialization of new fields with production defaults.

units.headline: GetRecord caches every lookup failure for 5 minutes per key
units.summary: Drops the retry parameter and moves fetching into c.get. Any error is now cached for errorCacheTTL and returned without asking the server again. That includes transient connection failures and timeouts, not only FORBIDDEN replies.
focus: Transient errors (dial failure, deadline exceeded) are cached for 5 minutes just like FORBIDDEN
Expired entries are removed only when the same key is looked up again
With loadMetadata now ignoring the error, items are tracked without an owner for the whole TTL

issues.title: Transient network errors cached for 5 minutes as if permanent
issues.failure_scenario: The inventory server restarts or a 1s request times out. connect() or conn.Get returns a non-ReplyError, and that key's error is cached. Every Track of that record for the next 5 minutes skips the lookup, and since loadMetadata swallows the error, items get no Owner even after the server recovers.

issues.title: Error cache never evicts keys that are not requested again
issues.failure_scenario: In a long-running process, every distinct key that fails once keeps its entry in c.errors for good unless that same key is requested again, so memory grows without bound.

units.reason: Changes retry and error semantics for every inventory lookup.

units.headline: Fetch reconnects once on transport errors, not on server error replies
units.summary: Moves the connect/get/retry logic out of GetRecord. It retries once after reconnecting, except when the error is a ReplyError. When the context deadline has passed, the retry reuses the same expired ctx.
focus: A retry after a timeout reuses the already-expired ctx, so the second attempt cannot succeed
Whether conn should also be closed on a ReplyError (it stays open by design)
units.reason: Rewrites retry and reconnect behavior against the inventory server.

units.headline: Adds helper that detects ReplyError via errors.As
units.summary: Small errors.As check for ReplyError, covered by TestIsErrorReply including the wrapped case. It only feeds the retry decision in fetchFromServer.
units.reason: Trivial helper that tests cover; its effect is judged in fetchFromServer.

units.headline: getRecord drops the removed retry argument from GetRecord call
units.summary: Call site updated to the new GetRecord signature. Retrying now happens inside fetchFromServer, so the behavior change belongs to the GetRecord and fetchFromServer units.
units.reason: Mechanical signature update; the behavior change belongs to other units.
